items.title: Norman Simmons interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 27, 2007 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Maybe people like Quincy and those people that came out there, and Cannonball. A lot of these guys met in the Army.

ctx.x: Did you end up doing the military?

No. No I was not in the military. When the next war came around, and I think it was the Korean War maybe, they were drafting — they were not drafting fathers — I mean they were not drafting husbands, and I had just gotten married. Then they started not drafting fathers and I had just had a kid. And I had my notice, bring enough clothes for three days, you know when you got that you were in the Army. They sent you this notice: bring it enough clothes for three days. That means you were in. I took that thing down…
That’s an interesting point. I hadn’t thought of that. Do you recall the first time you played in an integrated band? Or wasn’t it even something that would register in your memory?
